title: Washed disciples still need foot-washing; sanctify them in truth
source_text: XVII. Propterea Christus Dominus, loquens de illis qui sunt ipsius sanguine & spiritu abluti, Qui lotus est, inquit, non indiget nisi ut pedes lavet, sed est mundus totus. Joan. 13. Quibus verbis innuit illis ipsis qui sunt per ejus gratiam mundati & sanctificati, semper aliquid terrenarum sordium adhaerescere, a quo purgari & ablui debeant: quemadmodum illi qui corpus abluerunt, non possunt quin pedibus quibus terram contingunt, pulveris aliquid colligant, quo saltem illa parte contaminantur. Ideoque Patrem orat pro discipulis, quos jam ante mundos pronunciaverat, ut illos verbo suo sanctificet; Sanctifica, inquit, eos in veritate tua; verbum tuum est veritas. Joan. 17.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the Lord Christ, speaking of those who are washed by his blood and Spirit, says: He who is bathed needs only to wash his feet, but is wholly clean (John 13). By which words he hints that even to those who are cleansed and sanctified by his grace something of earthly filth always clings, from which they ought to be purged and washed: just as those who have washed the body cannot help collecting some dust with the feet by which they touch the earth, by which at least that part is contaminated. And therefore he prays the Father for the disciples, whom he had already pronounced clean, that he would sanctify them by his word: Sanctify them in your truth; your word is truth (John 17).
pass_b_english: Even the blood-washed still gather foot-dust and need ongoing cleansing (John 13).
Christ prays the Father to sanctify already-clean disciples in the truth of the word (John 17).
